text:
anya: Hey, anyone seen this before? Our Python async client hangs on shutdown when token refresh triggers during inflight requests. app never exits, Ctrl+C no effect.

sahil: Can you paste a minimal repro? Is this FastAPI/uvicorn or a script?

anya: FastAPI + uvicorn, using httpx.AsyncClient as a singleton on app startup. Auth uses our sync token refresher which calls requests.post to the auth server. Repro attached below.

anya: ```py
# simplified
from fastapi import FastAPI
import httpx
import time

app = FastAPI()
client = httpx.AsyncClient()  # created at import/startup

def get_token_sync():
    # calls requests.post (blocking) to refresh token
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return "tkn"

class SyncAuth(httpx.Auth):
    def auth_flow(self, request):
        token = get_token_sync()
        request.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
        yield request

client.auth = SyncAuth()

@app.get("/ping")
async def ping():
    r = await client.get("https://httpbin.org/delay/1")
    return {"status": r.status_code}
```

anya: If many requests come in and the token expires, the sync get_token_sync blocks inside the auth hook and things pile up. On shutdown uvicorn waits for tasks but these threads are blocked and the process doesn't exit cleanly.

liam: That makes sense — using a sync auth flow with AsyncClient will block the async loop because auth_flow runs in the same task. httpx expects AsyncAuth or you must offload blocking code.

maya: Do you see any explicit exception like "Event loop is closed" or just hang?

anya: Just hangs. No traceback. Ctrl+C shows "Waiting for application shutdown" forever.

sahil: Two quick fixes: 1) make token refresh async (use httpx.AsyncClient to call the auth endpoint) and implement AsyncAuth with async_auth_flow, or 2) wrap blocking refresh with anyio.to_thread.run_sync in the auth hook so it doesn't block the event loop.

liam: Example of option 2:
```py
import anyio
class BridgeAuth(httpx.Auth):
    async def async_auth_flow(self, request):
        token = await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(get_token_sync)
        request.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
        yield request
```

maya: Also make sure AsyncClient is closed on shutdown: await client.aclose(). Uvicorn shutdown can be racy if you rely on GC to close sockets.

anya: Nice, trying anyio workaround now. One more question: our SDK exposes a convenience sync token manager that a lot of users use. Should the Python SDK detect AsyncClient and switch to an async token flow automatically?

sahil: We discussed this in the SDK design doc — auto-detecting runtime could be surprising. Better: provide both sync and async token manager classes and clear docs on using them with AsyncClient vs Client. Maybe a helper that wraps the sync manager into an async adapter (to_thread) with a warning.

liam: Agree. Also add a runtime check that logs a WARN if a sync auth/refresh function is used while an AsyncClient is instantiated — help users discover the misconfig.

maya: Could add a test in CI that spins up an AsyncClient and asserts no blocking calls in the auth path (hard to test reliably but could be smoke).

anya: anyio.to_thread fixed the hang locally, thanks. I'll open a PR with docs + an "AsyncAdapter" helper for sync token providers and add a runtime warn.

ops-bot: created ticket #INFR-412: "python-sdk: document async token managers + add Sync->Async adapter"

sahil: Awesome. Also add a short note in the migration guide about not doing asyncio.run inside auth code — that triggers "RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop" in deployed apps.

anya: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
